# Recreation Prompt

Recreate **VaporRizz Parkour.exe**, a portrait-first browser parkour game inspired by vaporwave Y2K internet culture. Preserve the original first-person raycast parkour mechanics: generated elevated course, joystick/WASD movement, touch-look/arrow look, tap/Space jump, wall blocking, grounded lava-gap failure, goal-row success, speed and distance HUD, start/play/end/restart flow.

Transform the presentation into a satirical meme-skill commute run. The player is an anonymous `Ｒ` clip-runner farming clean rooftop uploads. Hazards are glitch gaps and 404 floor tiles. Walls are algorithm rails and meme billboards. The goal is an upload gate / ez clap clear. Use neon magenta, cyan, purple void, vapor sun, perspective grid, floating sticker copy, pixel HUD counters, and compact mobile CTAs. Keep one-thumb mobile play readable in 4:7 to 9:16 portrait.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
The source game is a browser-native first-person raycast parkour runner. The player starts on a generated elevated corridor, moves with WASD or a left virtual stick, looks/turns with arrow keys or the touch-look zone, and jumps with Space or the right jump button. The map uses tile codes: safe floor, wall blockers, lava/gap hazards, and a terminal goal row. The protected loop is start -> generated course -> active traversal -> lava failure or goal success -> restart.

## Protected mechanic truth
- Input semantics: drag/look, stick/WASD movement, Space/tap jump.
- Movement/update loop: raycast first-person traversal with fixed gravity and jump impulse.
- Collision: walls block horizontal movement; hazard tiles only fail when grounded; goal tile wins when grounded.
- Scoring/progress: speed and forward distance are displayed as live HUD values.
- State flow: start overlay, play HUD/controls, game-over/win overlay, restart.

## Remix target
The rebuilt game is **VaporRizz Parkour.exe**, a satirical vaporwave/Y2K mobile parkour game about an anonymous clip-farming rooftop runner uploading a clean commute run through meme billboards, glitch gaps, and neon algorithm rails. It preserves the source mechanics while transforming HUD language, focal identity, scene ownership, feedback, palette, and mobile presentation.

## Safe transformation surfaces
Visual and semantic surfaces are aggressively transformed: title, copy, HUD labels, button language, overlay design, procedural background motifs, canvas colors, floor/hazard/goal treatment, feedback tone, and catalog-backed fonts/GIF/audio references. Core mechanics are not rewritten.
